title: Recovery Survival Network: $11.2 million from the City, a board of one on its tax returns

beats.text: Recovery Survival Network, in San Francisco, houses and supports people leaving jail or on probation.

visual.label: Recovery Survival Network
visual.sub: housing and support for people leaving jail or on probation

beats.text: Since fiscal 2019, what have Adult Probation and the Sheriff’s Office paid it?

visual.label: City vouchers, fiscal 2019 to 2027 to date

beats.text: This is a lead, not a finding. Nothing here shows City money was misused.

visual.line: This is a lead, not a finding: a pattern in public records. This film says what the records show, what they do not show, and what would settle it.

beats.text: Its federal returns for 2020 to 2024 each list one voting board member.

visual.text: one voting member of the governing body; independent voting members: zero

beats.text: How many independent?

visual.text: one voting member of the governing body; independent voting members: zero

beats.text: None. And one person is listed in all: the executive director.

visual.label: voting member on every return, 2020 to 2024
visual.sub: zero independent; one person listed, the executive director

beats.text: Of 478 City-paid organizations with returns on file, it is the only one.

visual.label: 478 City-paid organizations
visual.sub: the only one with a single voting member on every return

beats.text: No conflict policy, no whistleblower policy, no minutes. The executive director reviews the return.
The City holds a different list of who runs it.
Sheriff’s Office notices from 2020 and 2022 name up to four directors,

b: up to 4 directors, a chief executive and a chief financial officer

beats.text: plus a chief executive and a chief financial officer.

b: up to 4 directors, a chief executive and a chief financial officer

beats.text: Those notices list who may not give to the official who approves the contract.

visual.line: the list of people barred from giving to the official who approves the contract

beats.text: Either the notices or the returns must be wrong. The records don’t show which.

visual.line: the list of people barred from giving to the official who approves the contract

beats.text: The notices’ finance chief shares the director’s surname; the records don’t show if they’re family.

visual.label: The same surname
visual.sub: the records do not show whether two people with the same surname are family

beats.text: Every return reports a loan from the executive director, to meet cash flow. How much?

steps.name: Recovery Survival Network
steps.sub: no board approval, no written agreement

beats.text: 34,541 dollars, the same each year. No board approval, no written agreement.

visual.label: the same on every return, 2020 to 2024
visual.sub: not approved by the board; no written agreement

beats.text: Yet the balance-sheet line for officer loans sits below zero at four of five year-ends.

visual.label: of five year-ends: loans from officers below zero

beats.text: On its face, that means the officer owes the organization. The return doesn’t say which.

visual.label: of five year-ends: loans from officers below zero

beats.text: Every return says its statements were neither compiled, reviewed nor audited.
Yet the Controller’s monitors, for fiscal 2023-24, recorded its audit as complete and on time.
Either an audit exists that the return denies, or the monitors marked it met without one.

visual.line: the City’s monitors marked audit standards as met without one
visual.kicker: Or an audit exists that the return denies

beats.text: The City’s business register lists three businesses under the executive director’s name, at the organization’s suite.

visual.label: 2940 16th Street, Suite 304
visual.sub: and 3012 16th Street: 3 business names under the executive director’s name

beats.text: Music touring and music businesses. The returns report no dealings with them.

visual.label: music touring, music
visual.sub: the returns report no business dealing with them

beats.text: A preparer may have answered the governance questions wrongly; the monitors may have accepted a compilation.

visual.line: a preparer who fills in the governance questions wrongly

beats.text: Nothing here shows money misused, or which record of the board is right.

cards: Which record of the board is right

beats.text: What would settle it? The audits the monitors received, and the board roster in Adult Probation’s files.

cards.what: The audits the Controller’s monitors received
The board roster and minutes in Adult Probation’s grant files

beats.text: No regulator has ruled on its board or its books.
A lead is a question, not an accusation.
